name: Evans Notch Dispersed Primitive Camping - White Mountain National Forest

management_agency.name: U.S. Forest Service - Saco Ranger District / Androscoggin District

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No fees, no permits required for general dispersed forest camping
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted on national forest lands at least 200 feet from roads, trails, and bodies of water. Prohibited within Forest Protection Areas (developed recreation sites).

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Cathole method: dig 6-8 inches deep in forest topsoil, at least 200 feet from streams and ponds. Pack out toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace. Black bears active in WMNF: bear canister or hard-sided vehicle food storage mandatory.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Gather dead and downed wood only.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires in established rock fire rings only. Extinguish cold to touch with stream water.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Obey Maine Forest Service burn danger warnings.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Paved state highway changing to unpaved gravel forest road (ME-113 / FS 12)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Narrow paved scenic road with seasonal winter closure; gravel side forest roads have washboards and frost heaves.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Normal low clearance front wheel drive car (accessible along ME-113 and main gravel turnouts in summer/fall)

nomad_connectivity_rating.verizon_reliability: 2-3 bars 4G LTE on open mountain slopes; weak in deep notch valleys
nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Moderate to High (Steep White Mountain ridges restrict line of sight)

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: May thaw: cool (45-60°F), high blackfly season (late May to June), high stream flow.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: 70-80°F, pleasant mountain climate, lush green canopy, cool nights (50-55°F).
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: World-famous New England autumn foliage (50-65°F daytime, 30-40°F nights), prime camping season.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Severe northern winter (10-30°F), heavy snowpack, ME-113 closed to wheeled vehicles (snowmobile trail).

dangers_and_hazards: Black Bears active throughout White Mountain NF - bear-proof food storage mandatory
Moose on ME-113 highway during dusk/dawn
Blackflies and mosquitoes in late spring/early summer

common_animals: Common Loon (Gavia immer on nearby lakes)

human_demographics_and_culture: White Mountains hikers, autumn leaf peepers, fly anglers, digital nomads, and overland explorers.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Abenaki indigenous traditions revere the White Mountains ('Wobanadenok' - the White Rocks) as sacred dwellings of the Creator and high sky spirits.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Glacial mountain stream energy, high atmospheric clarity, peaceful northern forest sanctuary.

nearby_hiking_trails.features: Open granite mountain summit views, waterfalls, alpine birch forest

public_reviews_summary: Extremely peaceful free primitive camping in Western Maine. Outstanding autumn scenery and reliable cell service near the main notch corridor.
other_data: Bortle Class 2 night sky. Abundant firewood.

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 38-52°F, ice-out on Maine lakes, black fly season in June.
